sections.content: How many people are non-commissioned officers and other ranks?

70,495 people

Listed their occupation as "Non-commissioned officers and other ranks" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Those holding jobs in this unit group are full-time members of the armed forces of the UK, the Commonwealth and other foreign countries and perform military duties for which there is no civilian equivalent.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "non-commissioned officers and other ranks", there were more men than women, (92.2% compared with 7.8%).

This is different compared with the average for the wider occupation group of "protective service occupations".

Men made up 92.2% and women made up 7.8% of "non-commissioned officers and other ranks"
Across the whole working population, 52% are men and 48% are women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to non-commissioned officers and other ranks included:

  • Marine and waterways transport operatives
  • Forestry and related workers
  • Aerospace engineers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women is most equally split:

  • Quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • Chartered and certified accountants
  • Conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "non-commissioned officers and other ranks" has a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 10.3% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as non-commissioned officers and other ranks, 33.7% were in this age group. The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "non-commissioned officers and other ranks" was 65 years and over.
